variables.name: light
variables.description: Oil-lamp reserve. Decreases by 1 at each of three lit-shortcut checkpoints (a culvert, a failing stope, a slab-choked drift). Reachable set at the tower is {0,1,2,3}; read only in ending prose flavor, not gated by condition (the transmitter/trust gates carry the finale).

variables.name: trust
variables.description: Dell Voss's confidence in you, built at three checkpoints where you look out for Dell over yourself (a failing rail, a catwalk gap, a switchback). Reachable set at the tower is {0,1,2}. Gates the finale's second resolution: trust==2 opens the together ending, ==1 a creditable solo ending, ==0 the estranged ending, on both the fixed and flare branches.

variables.name: transmitter
variables.description: Whether you recovered the tower's spare valve, wedged behind a rockfall at exactly one node partway down. Both values are reachable at the tower. Gates the finale's first resolution: true opens the clean-call branch, false forces the improvised flare branch.

nodes.body: The last boat left the docks two hours ago. The ash cloud the geologists said would come at midnight is already piling dark over the volcano's shoulder. Pika's lantern beam finds you at the field station gate. The survey crew is three days late. The cable station past the cooling fields is the only working line left on the island. The wind is starting to sound like something breathing.

Pika lays a hand on the chain-link gate and does not swing it open yet. Three routes cross the cooling fields to the cable station: the old lava bench that runs above the vents, the steam-cut gully where the runoff channel used to be, and the service road the relay masts follow. Whatever you pick tonight, you are stuck with it before you take ten steps.

choices.label: Take the lava bench above the vents.

nodes.body: The lava bench steps down in broken black crust. It is easy underfoot but loud. Every step scrapes glassy rock downhill, and the vents below hiss back at you like something keeping count.

choices.label: Pick up the pace and burn lamp oil.
Move slow, feel your way, save fuel.
Pick up the pace and burn lamp oil.

nodes.body: The steam-cut gully snakes through the old runoff channel. The mineral water is ankle-deep and stays corpse-cold no matter how many vents steam fifty yards to either side. Every step breaks a skin of sulfur crust you cannot see until you are already through it.

choices.label: Move slow, feel your way, save fuel.
Pick up the pace and burn lamp oil.
Move slow, feel your way, save fuel.

nodes.body: The service road is a relic of the island's first relay build. It is a packed cinder track with steel lattice masts tilting at every other rise. The nearest one lists so far starboard that its shadow in your lamp beam looks like a man bent double.

choices.label: Pick up the pace and burn lamp oil.
Move slow, feel your way, save fuel.
Pick up the pace and burn lamp oil.

nodes.body: The bench craters under each stride but you push hard. The lamp burns high and steady. Pika is two steps ahead, tracing the safe line from memory of a route walked once in daylight three years ago.
You pick across the bench like you are walking a frozen lake. You test each crust before your weight follows. The ash settling on your shoulders is the only company the dark lets through behind you.

You splash through the gully at a dead run. The mineral water is searing cold around your shins. You trust the lamp to find every dry stone before you land on it, because slowing down now means wading alone in the dark.

You read every stone with your soles before you trust it, and the cold stays exactly as mean and exactly as patient the whole wade down. The ash has not reached the gully floor yet, and the silence down here is a different kind of heavy.
You run the service road under the lean of the nearest mast. You do not look up at the insulator stack still hanging by a single bolt forty feet overhead. The bolt holds.
You keep to the cable trench and well clear of the mast's old lean radius. It is the longer arc around the cinder field but the one Pika tracks with a single nod you almost miss in the dark.
A rope ladder lashed across a vent mouth bars the way down; the rungs are slick with condensed steam, and Pika's lamp never wavers from you as you reach for the first one.
A lava tube, half blocked by old rubble, bars the way down. Pick a path through it, and the vents breathe out hot sulphur that tastes like a lit match held under your tongue.
A cable trench turned to warm mud bars the way down. Stay on the firm edge and move fast. Pika checks the survey map by touch, because looking away from you is not yet an option.
A skylight shaft, with slabs of fallen basalt roof, bars the way down. Duck the low plates and count your breaths. As you slip through the first gap, Pika's lamp never wavers from you.

nodes.body: The station stair spirals up the outside of the old relay hut. It is rusted through in spots where the sea wind catches it. A cable port hangs open at the top.

The cable room is just as the crew left it. A line amplifier valve has been missing from the set since the day it failed. Whether you are holding that valve or empty-handed decides everything that happens next.

choices.label: Seat the valve you carried across the field.
Strip the lamp and rig a flare instead.

nodes.body: The valve seats clean on the first try and the set hums back to life under your hands, the old signal light blinking green for the first time in three days.
With no valve to fit, you strip the lamp for its last oil and rig a flare off the station rail instead, the wick spent on one single throw against the advancing cloud.
The set is live and the call will go through clean, but what comes back over it, and whether Pika is still beside you to hear it, depends on the whole night behind you now.

choices.label: Trust carried you both this far.

nodes.body: The flare is one shot into a sky already grey with ash, and whether anyone is watching for it, and whether Pika still trusts your aim, depends on the whole night behind you now.

choices.label: Trust carried you both this far.

nodes.body: The call goes through clean. So does everything you did to earn it. Pika keys the second channel without being asked. Between you, the whole crew's coordinates go out clear. The mainland dispatch answers before the ash cloud even finishes stacking over the volcano's shoulder.

The call goes through and rescue is moving. Pika stands a little apart at the rail while you make it, glad of the result and still weighing the night it took to get here — the lamp's last oil burned somewhere your memory will not name yet.

The call goes through, and it is the only thing that does. Pika went back for the field station two hours ago and you send the crew's coordinates out to an empty relay room with nobody beside you to hear the dispatch answer.

Pika has the timing of the ash cloud in a way you never could, and calls the exact second to loose the flare. It clears the ridge and hangs for a long orange breath above the cooling field, and someone, somewhere below the fall line, is already watching for it.

The flare clears the ridge and burns for its ten seconds against the cloud. Whether it was seen is a question the night does not answer either way before you have to climb back down onto ground that will not hold still much longer.

The flare goes up alone. It is badly timed against a gust that was never going to give you a clean throw. It is gone into the ash with nothing behind it. No one is left on the ridge to have watched for it.
